title: Scott-continuous lambda models with theory \(\lambda \beta\)
formal: Does there exist a pointed directed-complete partial order D and Scott-continuous maps \(F:D\to [D\to D]\) and \(\mathrm{L}:[D\to D]\to D\) with \(F\circ \mathrm{L}=id\) such that, for every pair of finite untyped lambda terms M,N, equality of their interpretations for every environment in D holds if and only if M and N are beta-convertible?
why: A foundational completeness question for denotational semantics: does the mathematical structure used to describe approximation and recursion inevitably identify programs beyond beta-conversion, or can it preserve every distinction made by that computation rule?
status_note: The exact question is explicit in Honsell’s primary statement. A search through 11 September 2026 found no resolution of its \(\lambda \beta\) alternative. The inspected 2025–2026 filter-model papers study unsolvables and other equational theories. Proofs were not independently verified.
review_note: Individually developed from the primary problem statement, the effective-model theorem and 2025–2026 filter-model papers. This review checks their statements and scope, not their proofs.

progress.text: Honsell records the exact \(\lambda \beta\) and \(\lambda \beta \eta\) continuous-model questions, tracing discussion to the 1980s. This card asks the \(\lambda \beta\) alternative.
Berline, Manzonetto and Salibra rule out exact \(\lambda \beta\) and \(\lambda \beta \eta\) theories for their class of effective models.
Dezani-Ciancaglini, Giannini and Honsell analyze nontrivial interpretations of unsolvable terms in filter models.
Lambda Galore constructs sensible continuously complete filter models not extending Böhm-tree theory; sensibility prevents these constructions from realizing exactly \(\lambda \beta\).

category_assignment.reason: Category from the approved fundamental-problem proposal

definitions: Terms are generated by variables from a countably infinite set, application MN and abstraction \(\lambda x\).M, modulo renaming bound variables. Beta-convertibility is the least equivalence relation closed under application and abstraction containing (\(\lambda x\).M)\(N=M[N/x]\), with capture-avoiding substitution. A directed set is nonempty and every two of its elements have an upper bound in the set. D is a set with a partial order, a least element, and a supremum for every directed subset. Scott-continuous means monotone and preserving directed suprema. \([D\to D]\) consists of all Scott-continuous functions, ordered pointwise. An environment \(\rho\) assigns an element of D to each variable. Interpret x as \(\rho (x), MN\) as F(⟦M⟧\(\rho\))(⟦N⟧\(\rho\)), and \(\lambda x\).M as L(\(d\mapsto\)⟦M⟧\((\rho [x:=d])\)). The desired condition is \(\forall M,N\): (\(\forall \rho\), ⟦M⟧\(\rho\)=⟦N⟧\(\rho\)) ⇔ \(M=\beta N\). Models need not be countable, algebraic, effectively presented or extensional; in particular \(\mathrm{L}\circ F=id\) is not required. These are set-based directed-complete orders and all their continuous maps, without a restriction to graph models.
answer_criterion: Prove that a pointed dcpo and continuous retraction F,L satisfying the stated exact-theory condition exist, or prove that none exist. A negative answer must cover all such dcpos, without assuming an effective presentation, algebraicity or extensionality.

sentences: Scott's continuous semantics interprets untyped lambda terms using mathematical domains and continuous functions.
The project asks whether some model identifies exactly the pairs of terms related by beta-conversion.
Beta-conversion expresses equality generated by applying functions to arguments and substituting those arguments into their bodies.
Many semantic constructions validate additional equations, so soundness for beta-reduction alone does not answer the question.
An exact model would show whether this influential notion of continuous meaning can distinguish every pair of terms that the basic operational equations keep separate.

upgraded_from.title: Scott-continuous model with exactly λβ equational theory

context_blocks.text: The untyped lambda calculus describes functions using variables, application and abstraction. Beta-reduction substitutes an argument into a function body. A denotational model assigns mathematical meanings to terms and makes every beta-conversion valid. The question asks whether continuity can coexist with complete precision: no two terms should become equal in the model unless beta-conversion already equates them.

In domain semantics, an order represents increasing information and a directed supremum combines compatible approximations. Scott continuity requires functions to preserve these suprema. The map L represents each continuous self-map by an element of D, and F turns an element back into its associated self-map. The equation \(F\circ \mathrm{L}=id\) ensures that interpreting function application recovers the represented function. This makes beta-reduction sound.

Representability is a semantic condition. The element representing a continuous function need not be denoted by any finite lambda term. Requiring every continuous function to have a finite program would change the question. The model need not have computable elements, a computable ordering or a computable interpretation algorithm.

Extensional equality makes an additional identification. If x is not free in f, eta-conversion equates \(\lambda x\).f x with f, although these terms need not be beta-convertible. Imposing \(\mathrm{L}\circ F=id\) would validate this extra equality. This card therefore requires only the retraction in the other direction and keeps the beta-eta version as a separate target.

Quotienting syntax by beta-conversion gives a term model with exactly the desired equality. It does not automatically provide a pointed dcpo representing all continuous self-maps. The issue is whether the exact syntactic theory can be realized in this particular semantic setting.

Berline, Manzonetto and Salibra prove that the effective models defined in their paper cannot have theory exactly \(\lambda \beta\) or \(\lambda \beta \eta\). They also prove non-enumerability of the order theory, which records inequalities between denotations. Equational theory records equalities instead. A theorem restricted to effective models, or to order rather than equality, cannot be generalized silently to arbitrary dcpos.

Divergent terms reveal another source of extra equations. A term is unsolvable when no finite reduction exposes a head normal form: an outer variable applied to arguments after any leading abstractions. A sensible model equates all unsolvable closed terms. This is stronger than beta-conversion, which distinguishes some of them. The 2025 filter-model paper studies when unsolvables receive nontrivial interpretations and which type-theoretic conditions govern that behavior.

Lambda Galore, published in 2026, constructs sensible filter models representing all continuous functions whose theories do not contain the full Böhm-tree theory. It separates two semantic properties and resolves a different question about models. Sensibility still identifies unsolvables, so these constructions do not realize exactly \(\lambda \beta\). Continuous representability alone does not make their equational theory the one requested here.
